# `sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink`

**No jQuery call that parses a built string as HTML**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-security-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-security-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `sanitizers` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (whether the value is text or markup is a decision for the author) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Security** | CWE-79 · OWASP A05:2025 · security severity `high` |

## What it checks

jQuery's `.html(x)` is not given a value that is not a literal, and `$(x)`, `.append(x)`, `.prepend(x)`, `.after(x)`, `.before(x)`, `.replaceWith(x)` and `.wrap(x)` are not given a template or concatenation that holds a tag.

**Your sanitizer:** a value passes when it is a call to one of the `sanitizers`: the built-in list (DOMPurify, sanitize-html, xss, escape-html, lodash and he `escape`, Trusted Types `createHTML`) plus your own, each matched by name and by the module it is imported from, so a local `function sanitize(x) { return x }` does not pass. `sanitizers_mode = "replace"` makes yours the only ones that count. It does not follow a value through a variable: `const c = clean(x)` then `c` at the sink is not a call. Add a project function with `sanitizers = [{ name = "sanitizeHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]`.

**Why:** These calls parse their argument as HTML, so markup in a value built into it runs in the page (CWE-79).

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-security-js
pip install codelaw-rules-security-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:sec-js/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sanitizers` | `call[]` | 10 entries (below) | functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count |
| `sanitizers_mode` | `string` | `"extend"` | `extend` adds your `sanitizers` to the default list; `replace` uses only yours |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink"]
severity = "error"

[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "DOMPurify.sanitize", module = ["dompurify", "isomorphic-dompurify"] }, "DOMPurify.sanitize", { name = "sanitizeHtml", module = "sanitize-html" }, { name = "xss", module = "xss" }, { name = "filterXSS", module = "xss" }, { name = "escapeHtml", module = "escape-html" }, { name = "escape", module = ["lodash", "lodash-es", "lodash/escape", "he"] }, { name = "_.escape", module = ["lodash", "lodash-es"] }, { name = "he.escape", module = "he" }, "*.createHTML"]
sanitizers_mode = "extend"
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = { severity = "error", options = { sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep, except a `call[]` option in `extend` mode, which adds to it.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `sanitizers`

*call[]* · default: the list below

functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
```

**The default list** — a callee path (a global, `*.` for any receiver) or `{ name, module }`, held only when imported from that module:

```toml
sanitizers = [
  { name = "DOMPurify.sanitize", module = ["dompurify", "isomorphic-dompurify"] },
  "DOMPurify.sanitize",
  { name = "sanitizeHtml", module = "sanitize-html" },
  { name = "xss", module = "xss" },
  { name = "filterXSS", module = "xss" },
  { name = "escapeHtml", module = "escape-html" },
  { name = "escape", module = ["lodash", "lodash-es", "lodash/escape", "he"] },
  { name = "_.escape", module = ["lodash", "lodash-es"] },
  { name = "he.escape", module = "he" },
  "*.createHTML",
]
```

**Only yours count** — a direct call to a default entry is then reported:

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
sanitizers_mode = "replace"
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/security-js/rules/sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### extend: the project function passes

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
```

```js
import { cleanHtml } from "@acme/security";
$(el).html(cleanHtml(x));
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### extend: the built-in DOMPurify still passes

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
```

```js
import DOMPurify from "dompurify";
$(el).html(DOMPurify.sanitize(x));
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### replace: the project function passes

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
sanitizers_mode = "replace"
```

```js
import { cleanHtml } from "@acme/security";
$(el).html(cleanHtml(x));
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### replace: DOMPurify is reported

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
sanitizers_mode = "replace"
```

```js
import DOMPurify from "dompurify";
$(el).html(DOMPurify.sanitize(x));
```

**Reports** at `2:1`.

#### an aliased import passes

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
```

```js
import { cleanHtml as clean } from "@acme/security";
$(el).html(clean(x));
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a function of the same name from another module is reported

```toml
[rules."sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink".options]
sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]
```

```js
import { cleanHtml } from "left-pad";
$(el).html(cleanHtml(x));
```

**Reports** at `2:1`.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = { options = { sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink" = { severity = "warn", options = { sanitizers = [{ name = "cleanHtml", module = "@acme/security" }] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"sanitizers": [{"name": "cleanHtml", "module": "@acme/security"}]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule sec-js/no-jquery-html-sink  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>              # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Use `.text(value)` to write a value as text.
2. Build elements with `$("<li>").text(name)` and append them, rather than concatenating markup.
3. Where markup is needed, pass the value through a sanitizer (`DOMPurify.sanitize`) first.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
$("#out").html(comment.body);
$("#list").append("<li>" + name + "</li>");
```

#### Do

```js
$("#out").text(comment.body);
$("#list").append($("<li>").text(name));
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
$("#out").html(comment.body);
$("#list").append("<li>" + name + "</li>");
```

#### Do

```jsx
$("#out").text(comment.body);
$("#list").append($("<li>").text(name));
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
$("#out").html(comment.body);
$("#list").append("<li>" + name + "</li>");
```

#### Do

```ts
$("#out").text(comment.body);
$("#list").append($("<li>").text(name));
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
$("#out").html(comment.body);
$("#list").append("<li>" + name + "</li>");
```

#### Do

```tsx
$("#out").text(comment.body);
$("#list").append($("<li>").text(name));
```
